name: Mid-America Apartment Communities, Inc.
moat_justification: Scale, platform and cheap long-dated capital are real but modest advantages in a commodity business: apartments have no network effects, no lock-in beyond a 12-month lease and no pricing power against new supply (new-lease rates -5.3% in Q2 2026). Filed returns confirm it — ROE ~8-11% recently, not the sustained well-above-cost-of-capital record a 7+ moat requires. Moat 4/10 (weak).

one_liner: Quality Sun Belt apartment REIT, moat 4/10 — scale, expense discipline and a 4.5x-levered balance sheet are real, but apartments are a commodity with no pricing power against new supply (new-lease rates -5.3% in Q2 2026, same-store NOI guided negative for 2026); on a TTM owner's-earnings base of $5.76/share after charging filed capital-improvements capex, weighted IRR is 7.5% (IV@15% $46.51) at $116.63, so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$47 — the REIT lens (FY2026 Core FFO guided at $8.53/share, DPS TTM $6.075) is kinder than the OE lens, but neither supports 15% at this price.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Scale: ~105,000 units across 16 Sun Belt states — the largest apartment REIT platform, with in-house development, redevelopment and renovation capability (interior renovations earning ~25% cash-on-cash, Q2 2026 call)
Operating platform and expense discipline: same-store opex growth held to ~80-90 bps YoY through Q2 2026 while revenue fell, record-low resident turnover of 39.6% and renewal pricing +5.2%
Balance-sheet strength as a competitive tool: net debt/EBITDA ~4.5x, ~6-year average maturity at a 3.9% effective rate (Q2 2026 call) — cheaper, longer capital than private landlords
Diversified Sun Belt footprint across primary and mid-tier markets cushions single-market supply shocks (mid-tier markets outperforming high-supply ones in 2026)
moat_against: Apartments are a commodity product — Q2 2026 new-lease rates were -5.3% under Sun Belt oversupply, proving no pricing power when supply lands
Low tenant switching costs; leases are 12-month and residents can move to a competing new property with concessions
Returns are capped by replacement cost / cap-rate arbitrage — new supply is the permanent competitor
ROE has run only ~8-11% in recent years (fundamentals.json) and the roic_proxy series is not computable from the filed presentation — no evidence of sustained returns well above the cost of capital
Sun Belt concentration: the same migration markets (Austin, Phoenix, Charlotte, Nashville) took the record supply wave
